messages:
sara (runtime): quick summary: ran a focused microprofile across a 2-node setup with mixed NVLink/PCIe connectivity. saw consistent all-reduce tail latency when TP=4 PP=2 and small per-step microbatches. attaching observations below.

miguel (hw): curious — is this the NVLink-star config or the hybrid where 1 GPU pair is NVLink and the other crosses PCIe?

sara (runtime): hybrid. nodeA has full NVLink mesh, nodeB is a PCIe-only instance. baseline perf was fine on homogeneous racks, but once we mix, all-reduce stalls spike ~25-35% at the end of backward.

nina (infra): can you paste the perf counters / NCCL trace? even a short snippet helps. Also which kernel selections were in use?

sara (runtime): paste of ringtrace snippet (trimmed):

```
ALLREDUCE rank0->rank1: 1.1ms
ALLREDUCE rank1->rank0: 5.7ms  <-- long
KV_CACHE_PREFETCH: hit
KERNEL select: f16_matmul_v2 (vectorized)
KERNEL fallback: f16_matmul_generic
```

The long hop correlates with fallback kernel on the PCIe side and a subsequent stall waiting for ring slot free.

devin (model-ops): interesting — small gradient sizes cause fragmentation. are we doing prefix caching that reduces data reuse so messages are many small chunks?

sara (runtime): yes, KV cache behavior changed after the recent prefix-opt patch. cache hits went up but the per-token message count also increased because the worker slices are smaller, so we went from 2 x 256KB messages to 8 x 64KB messages. more messages => all-reduce push/pop churn.

miguel (hw): that explains PCIe microbursting. NVLink pairs absorb a lot of small-message overhead with HW-level aggregation; PCIe suffers from PCIe-TLP inefficiencies. we should try coalescing at the runtime layer (batch-slice coalesce) before issuing NCCL ops.

sara (runtime): tried a quick experiment: increase batch-slice to 64KB and enable eager coalesce. result: tail latency drops ~12% but cost of kernel switch increased slightly (more memory pressure). logs: 
```
./scripts/comm_probe.sh --tp 4 --pp 2 --slice-kb 64 --coalesce=1
Result: tail 12% down, kernel-switch-rate +8% on PCIe node
```

nina (infra): we can also try changing NCCL tuning envs for heterogeneous fabric: NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0 NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 and NCCL_TOPO_DUMP=1 to verify path selection. also enable async progress to reduce blocking on user threads: NCCL_ASYNC_PROGRESS=1.

sara (runtime): tried NCCL_ASYNC_PROGRESS=1 — small improvement but not enough. suspect kernel selection still chooses a fallback generic matmul on the PCIe node causing compute skew and preventing overlap.

miguel (hw): idea: add a scheduling policy that biases comm-first on mixed-topology rings, i.e., prefer faster hops to initiate partial reductions while waiting for slow hops to drain. similar to staggered all-reduce where you pipeline chunks across ringlets.

devin (model-ops): would that change memory/KV cache invariants? if we pipeline more aggressively we may need more KV cache slots or risk eviction that affects quality. tradeoff.

sara (runtime): yup. sketch of proposed change: 1) detect heterogeneous link speeds per ring via topo probe; 2) compute per-chunk schedule that assigns earlier chunks to fast links, delayed chunks to slow links; 3) update kernel-selection heuristics to prefer kernels that minimize tail variance on slow devices (smaller tile kernels even if a slight FLOPS loss).

miguel (hw): I can add a microprobe to expose effective bandwidth and latency per peer (RDMA ping/throughput). output: JSON table we can ingest into the scheduler.

infra-bot: new perf-run uploaded: s3://perf/runs/2412345678/hybrid-topo-multipath/ — includes nvlink traces, PCIe counters, and NCCL traces.

nina (infra): thanks infra-bot. next action items:
- sara: implement a small simulator to compute chunk schedules (estimate time per-chunk = comm_time(peer, size) + compute_time(chunk_size)).
- miguel: add the per-peer microprobe and a CI check to run on mixed-hardware lab.
- devin: provide a small eval harness to test KV-cache impact on token quality when we increase chunking/pipelining.

sara (runtime): I'll drop a PR with a PoC of the scheduler and a short perf harness. expecting microbench numbers within 48h.

miguel (hw): FYI, also try toggling kernel selection threshold in the runtime: prefer vectorized kernel only if contiguous stride > 128 and available memory> X. that avoids the fallback penalty on PCIe.

sara (runtime): noted. will include that as a runtime flag.

devin (model-ops): if this works we should add a regression eval against our production prompt set — we can't sacrifice prompt latency variance for occasional throughput wins.

sara (runtime): agreed. will add end-to-end traces and a synthetic prompt sweep.

nina (infra): looping @eng-oncall for heads up on CI lab runs that will stress the mixed cluster tomorrow.

miguel (hw): thanks all. small next step: sara, drop the probe outputs into the perf run bucket and post link here.

sara (runtime): uploaded: s3://perf/runs/2412345678/hybrid-topo-multipath/probe.json and small trace tar. starting sim now.

infra-bot: job perf-sim-2412345678 started (ETA ~2h).
